walkthroughs.body_html:
Two main cold environments:

• Polar — Antarctica and Arctic ice; almost no plants
• Tundra — treeless; mosses, lichens, grasses; permafrost below

Both have extreme cold and low precipitation.

Cold environments share:

• Average winter temps below -30°C
• Very low precipitation (often <250 mm/yr)
• Short growing season (~50 days)
• 24h darkness/light seasonally

Effectively cold deserts.

Cold environments are fragile because:

• Slow plant growth = slow recovery
• Permafrost melts if disturbed
• Few species — simple food webs
• Slow nutrient cycling

Damage can last decades.

options: Permanent snow on hills
Ground frozen for 2+ years
Glaciers
Frozen rivers

mcqs.q: Which biome lies south of the tundra?
options: Savanna
Taiga (boreal forest)
Desert
Rainforest

mcqs.q: What is the difference between the tundra and the taiga biomes?
options: Meanders form because the river is going downhill very steeply.
Tundra and taiga are the same biome with different names.
Tundra is treeless cold biome (too cold and permafrost-dominated for trees), while taiga (boreal forest) is the band of coniferous forest just south of the tundra in subarctic latitudes.
Tundra is in the Arctic and taiga is in the Antarctic.

mcqs.q: Why do meanders migrate across a floodplain?
options: Sustainable development means using only solar power.
Faster water on the outside of the bend causes erosion (river cliff); slower water on the inside causes deposition (slip-off slope) — over time the channel shifts laterally.
Meanders form because the river is going downhill very steeply.
Meanders form because rivers flow around obstacles like rocks.
